policy.trigger: Relevant pinned CPU prefill allocation/fallback source change; no new Issue24 comment request
policy.input: same original trial-01 repeated three times
policy.forced_fallback_expectation: pin64 once-only pinned-host-buffer warning and zero prompt host experts for all3 requests; all requests finish2048 tokens. This configured cap simulates refusal; it is not OS RAM exhaustion or the original Windows crash.
policy.limits: No Windows20K/40K/89K reproduction, no long-context extension, no new numerical accuracy CHECK. Speed profiling separate from numerical checks. No extra artificial workload.

limitations: Host audit samples same-user process CPU/IO/RSS and all GPU compute PIDs every ~2 seconds, with whole-NVMe settling checks before each case; it cannot exclude every short OS event. CPU0 changes the intended prompt baseline, so band labels are descriptive. Diagnostic profiling adds CUDA events and synchronization. Every process runs three identical 16K/2K requests; the exit profiler includes the first warm-up and all subsequent prefill work. Stage event intervals are accumulated GPU stream time, may include stream stalls, and are not a pure kernel breakdown or a sum of end-to-end request wall time. Five fixed fresh starts (three default, one PIN_MB64, one CPU0) are a bounded verification sample, not an unbiased frequency estimate or a clean speed/quality comparison. Output IDs can differ; no new numerical CHECK run.
